title: Fantastic app, amazing customer service
body:
-I’ve been using AM for about 6 months. 

-I’ve tried loads of different project planning apps and tend to get a bit obsessive over getting my planning system perfect.

-AM is by far the best i’ve used. 

-On top of that, when i got in touch with customer service i got a quick friendly reply that completely solved the issue. 

-I honestly feel like they are trying to make life easier for their customers, not just in it for the money which is unusual and refreshing.

-100% would recommend if you want a central app to plan everything and anything in

Tip:
-The web interface is better than the app. I do all of the heavy editing on my laptop but use the app to add things on the fly.
author: DMMaddison

title: Glitch in calendar renders app almost useless
body:
This app is clever and customisable.  It doesn’t have much flexibility in its interface (you can’t fix the option buttons on tasks, raise text size on the wall, or stop the background changing colour as you mouse over, even in dark mode, which as a migraine sufferer, I find maddening - I don’t need more things moving and flashing) but it does allow a lot of customisation strategy - matrixes of more than one type, reminders, different ways of organising lists, time blocks for certain types of task (good for housework).  And it has evaluation tools like time tracking so you can see if you worked your plan.

However, there is no way of copying time blocks or appointments on the calendar.  It’s necessary to create each one individually, which takes ages.  It’s supposed to be possible to shift-click to copy, but a (confirmed) bug has stopped this working.  This has been left unfixed for months, leaving me struggling desperately with matching to-do with time, and rendering most advantages of the program (like time blocks) useless.  As most computer calendars have more than one route by which you can copy, that it should have been left unfixed for so long is unbelievable (if they can’t deal with the shift-click bug they can add other options for the function).  And any function being left broken is a breech of trust: what will go wrong next?  It’s recommended for neurodiversity but of all people we most need reliable functionality. 

All in all, my experience with this program has been a frustrating waste of time and energy.  It would be wonderful if it worked as it’s supposed to.  It doesn’t.
author: Floweringoctopus

title: Hidden gem!
body: I’ve just spent hours testing over 20 different productivity tools. I was ready to give up and stick with my old tool that although wasn’t perfect was free and familiar. Then I decided to try Marvin (I tested it last year and it wasn’t quite right). OMG! It’s absolutely amazing and meets all my needs. I hope my review will encourage others to try it (or try it again if you tried it previously). Together with the desktop app, this will now be my main productivity tool.
author: Danylko

title: Read the small print!
body: This is a very promising app, but the price is way to high. It is asking £10.39 a month! This information does not feature prominently, so before you go ahead and put all the effort in, consider if you want to pay that amount in perpetuity, or if there is other options out there. It’s a shame, because it looks good, but with that price point, I’d also ponder how long it will keep going, and what will happen to all your input if you leave/it stops.
author: Brette1979

title: Love this app!
body:
If you are looking for a customisable to-do app, then look no further. Amazing Marvin is powerful and lets you personalise your experience as you wish.

I also love the gamification of the app, even if I am a fully grown up person! 

Keep up the good work Marvin, you’re Amazing 😉

author: Xenopus15

title: Fabulous but will need desktop/ web for the best experience
body:
Amazing Marvin is quite simply amazing (despite the daft name). The web/desktop version is quite simply the most configurable and  flexible project management/ task manager on the market. Whatever you want it to be GTD- XYZ, it can do it. Yes, there is a learning curve, and yes, there are a few features I would like to see (location reminders!! 🗺) but you literally can make it as simple or as complicated as you like.

This iOS app is very much an addition - it gives some of the basic capability but not nearly all, but this is more than enough for task management when you are out and about. 

Amazing Marvin have a small but responsive dev team and they are incredibly responsive to customers. Overall a great product.

P. S. I have no financial or other interest in AM, except that I am a happy customer.
author: Orca1910

title: Amazing indeed
body: I have ADHD and I’m autistic. All todo apps have failed to keep me organised because of their lack of flexibility (which I need to keep up with my ever changing cognitive function). Marvin delivers that flexibility and more. Together with its web app, I can tailor my day based on how I feel. Just turn on and off different strategies. Procrastinating... got frogs. Struggling to get started... got pomodoro. Have brain fog and can’t function? Reschedule easily. The mobile app is a little more basic but still functions well enough to keep you going and I’ve seen plenty of evidence to know that the Dev team are on the ball and committed to making Marvin the day planning app we all need and deserve!
author: ImperfectlyVictoria
